slides.stem:
The experiment ______ the team learned more from it than they expected.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

slides.body: "The experiment failed" and "the team learned more from it" are both complete sentences, and a comma alone can't join them — that's the comma splice the SAT tests constantly. The semicolon joins them legally. No punctuation runs them together, and "however" with one comma strands the sentence.

slides.title: A comma can't join sentences
slides.body:
Two independent clauses need a period, a semicolon, or a comma plus a coordinating conjunction. "However" never rescues a comma — it needs a semicolon in front of it.

This exact boundary decision appears several times on every test.
